:::{#exr-epe-split-noise}
#### Separate the noise

Given a covariate value $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
the **noise** $\noise \eqdef \newoutvar - \truemeanfnf{\predvar}$
is the [deviation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean)
of the new outcome $\newoutvar$ from its [population mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) given $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
the [mean function](#def-mean-function) value $\truemeanfnf{\predvar}$.
So $\newoutvar = \truemeanfnf{\predvar} + \noise$,
and $\noise$ has population mean $0$
and [population variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) $\varpar \eqdef \Var{\noise}$,
which we take to be finite.
Suppose that the new pair $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$
is drawn from the same population as the observations in the random [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$,
and [independently](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) of $\trainset$.
Take every expectation below to be conditional on $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
Add and subtract $\truemeanfnf{\predvar}$ inside the square of the [expected prediction error](#def-epe),

$$
\E{\sqf{\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}}},
$$

expand it, and take the expectation term by term.

Two of the three terms simplify.
Say what each becomes,
and name which facts about the noise hold by definition
and which hypothesis makes the cross term zero.

:::
